subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.q: In a tree diagram, the first branch shows P = 0.6 and a following branch shows P = 0.5. What is the probability of both happening?
The probability of winning a game is 0.2. In 50 games, how many wins are expected?
Which value could NOT be a probability?
questions.explain: Probabilities lie between 0 and 1, so 1.2 is impossible.

questions.q: Two fair coins are flipped. What is P(both heads)?
On the probability scale, what value represents an impossible event?
In a Venn diagram, 5 people like tea only, 3 like coffee only and 2 like both, out of 12 people. How many like neither?
How many outcomes are in the sample space when rolling two fair six-sided dice?
A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is P(rolling a 4)?
questions.explain: There is one favourable outcome out of six equally likely: 1/6.

questions.q: Probabilities for three outcomes are 0.2, 0.5 and x. What is x?
A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. What is P(red)?
The probability it rains is 0.3. What is the probability it does not rain?
